Subject: AegisMed private hosting requirements — call recap & asks

Hi Sonia / Michael,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. I captured what we discussed and a few clarifying questions.

Key business drivers (what you told us):
- Regulatory & residency: patient PHI must remain within your US datacenter footprint; state residency constraints for CA and NY clinical records.
- Security posture: SOC 2 + HIPAA required; preference for HSM-backed KMS and no unmanaged remote access.
- Air-gap preference: pilot should run with limited egress; production might require fully isolated VPC or an on-prem air-gapped cluster.
- Integration needs: FHIR ingestion pipeline + HL7 adapters, and near-real-time inference (~500 TPS peak across many endpoints).

Technical constraints / asks you raised:
- No outbound internet from inference tier; approved jump-host or NAT review required.
- IP allowlist only; no DNS-based egress for model downloads.
- Certificate pinning for service-to-service TLS.
- Dedicated HSM or customer KMS integration (Azure Key Vault or AWS CloudHSM discussed).

Proposed scope for a pilot (what we recommended):
- Short pilot (6–8 weeks): isolated VPC deployment in AegisMed DC, limited dataset, metrics capture (latency, cost), and a security pen-test window.
- Deliverable: small production-like cluster, documented runbook for patching and incident escalation.

Open questions (please provide):
1) Network diagram showing firewall egress rules and jump-host details (requested as PDF).
2) Procurement timeline and any required PO/contract lead times.
3) Who is the technical owner for running the pilot (point name + on-call contact)?
4) Expected average and peak token volumes (approx. TPS/RPS for API calls).

Action items / owners: 
- Marcus (me) — capture contract & pricing baseline; prepare commercial MAP. Attachment: MAP_AegisMed_v0.3.xlsx
- Priyom Das (cc'd) — will scope the security/deep-dive call and prepare a checklist for HSM/KMS options.
- Ben Carter (cc'd) — will prepare preliminary commercial options (reserved capacity vs dedicated).
- AegisMed team — share network diagram and procurement contact.

Attachments: redwood_private_deployment_baseline.pdf (deployment checklist), MAP_AegisMed_v0.3.xlsx (mutual action plan template).

Suggested next steps:
- Security deep-dive + network walkthrough (45–60 min) — propose Wed 2026-07-22 or Thu 2026-07-23.
- Procurement sync (if available) the week after to align PO timeline.

If you can send the network diagram and procurement contact, we’ll use that to scope the pilot SOW and targeted timeline.

Thanks,

Marcus Lin

Marcus — thanks for the concise recap. Helpful. Quick answers inline and attached a rough network diagram (AegisMed_network_diagram_v1.pdf).

Inline:
- Network diagram: attached; inference compute sits in an isolated VLAN with no direct outbound. All outbound must go through our bastion/proxy cluster; we can provide NAT IPs for allowlisting.
- KMS/HSM: we currently run Azure Key Vault with HSM-backed keys for PHI workloads. We will need a proposal that supports integrating with our AKV or a customer-managed HSM.
- Egress policy: no model downloads from internet. Any model artifacts must be pushed from a secure staging host by our infra team.
- Certs: we can provide internal CA certs; we require cert pinning for any remote management endpoints.

Volume/throughput: average ~120 TPS; expected peaks up to ~600 TPS during batch ingest windows.

Procurement: procurement@aegismed.com (cc'd on this thread) handles PO/terms. Typical lead time for vendor onboarding and security review is 6–8 weeks.

Technical owner: Michael (IT Director) will be the primary point for infrastructure; Sonia will own clinical integration and data residency requirements.

Next step: I can make time for the security deep-dive on Thu 2026-07-23 10:00–11:00 PT. Please confirm and include Priyom and any SRE folks.

- Michael
